review_comments.body: **New assertions fail repository checks** The new tests use conditional `t.Fatalf` and `t.Errorf` calls throughout. `AGENTS.md` requires `testify` assertions, and `TestNoHandRolledAssertions` scans every Go test file for exactly this pattern. The repository-wide suite will fail even if the Bedrock package tests pass. Replace these checks with `require` for preconditions and `assert` for independent checks. The same pattern appears at lines 39–40 and 105–106, and elsewhere in this file. **Context Used:** AGENTS.md ([source](https://github.com/enterpilot/gomodel/blob/main/AGENTS.md))

** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Replace the manual precondition check with `require.NoError`.** The `if err != nil { t.Fatalf(...) }` block matches the hand-rolled assertion rule. `TestNoHandRolledAssertions` flags any `if` whose only action fails the test, so this file fails the normal test run. Use `require` for a precondition that later lines depend on, as the repository's testify convention requires. ```diff --- "a/internal/providers/bedrock/response_format_test.go" +++ "b/internal/providers/bedrock/response_format_test.go" @@ -28,9 +28,7 @@ const schema = `{"type":"object","properties":{"zeta":{"type":"string"},"alpha":{"type":"string"}},"additionalProperties":false}` parts, err := buildConverseParts(responseFormatRequest( `{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"answer","description":"the answer","strict":true,"schema":` + schema + `}}`)) - if err != nil { - t.Fatalf("buildConverseParts: %v", err) - } + require.NoError(t, err, "buildConverseParts") for name, config := range map[string]*brtypes.OutputConfig{ "converse": converseInput(parts).OutputConfig, ``` Apply the same change to the other manual `t.Fatalf` and `t.Errorf` checks in this file. Use `assert` for an independent check that does not guard a later dereference. Add the `github.com/stretchr/testify/require` import if it is missing.
